Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 0.65% to 23,146 on narrow participation
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +3.52% weighted by turnover, against +0.17% for the median stock, a gap of 3.4 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Shoppers Stop Limited fell 5.4% on 140 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Investor Presentation”.

Aurum PropTech Limited fell 2.8% on 79 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Investor Presentation”.

Orient Electric Limited rose 1.9% on 245 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Link of Recording”.

PTC India Financial Services Limited rose 4.1% on 86 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Bonus issues, stock splits & dividends: HDB Financial, IRFC, TechM among 19 stocks turning ex-record date this week”.

What happened
Breaking
Challenges ahead for Fairfax's management of IDBI Bank post ₹52,878 crore stake deal approval
Fairfax Financial acquired a 60.7% stake in IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore following regulatory approval. The takeover marks a key privatisation milestone that could re-rate IDBI Bank, though earnings upside depends on controlling employee expenses and legacy bad loans to maintain return metrics. Watch upcoming quarterly cost-to-income ratios to verify operational integration.
ET Markets · +2 others
Banks also count cost of insurance payout curbs
Proposed bancassurance payout caps will reduce Central Bank of India's insurance fee income by 33% and hit Canara Bank by ₹145 crore. The regulatory restriction directly compresses non-interest income margins across listed lenders, including Axis Bank and HDFC Bank. Final IRDAI guidelines on commission ceilings will determine the exact hit to FY26 earnings estimates.
ET Markets · +2 others
'India an important ally': Rubio says Trump studying effects of tariffs on countries like India
US Secretary of State nominee Marco Rubio stated the incoming US administration is evaluating the impact of proposed import tariffs on India. Reciprocal tariffs would directly hit export demand across listed Indian textiles, IT services, and auto ancillary companies, while pressuring the rupee. Specific trade policy announcements following the US presidential inauguration will confirm duty structures.

Who is Amal Kelshikar? Why did he resign from the position of Torrent Pharmaceuticals' Executive Director? Explained
Torrent Pharmaceuticals Executive Director Amal Kelshikar submitted his resignation, with his exit scheduled two years ahead in October 2026. The extended leadership transition avoids immediate operational disruption, leaving Torrent's high-margin domestic formulation business intact. Board appointments over the coming year will indicate the company's long-term succession strategy.

Your themes
Dee Development signs framework pact with EPC firm for nuclear power - scanx.trade
DEE Development Engineers entered a framework agreement with an unnamed EPC contractor to supply high-pressure nuclear piping packages. Nuclear-grade piping carries higher gross margins than conventional thermal or oil piping due to stringent safety qualifications and limited domestic competition. The pact strengthens order book visibility for DEE's specialized fabrication yard as state fleet orders for heavy water reactors ramp up.
NuclearNuclear and SMR · +1 other
Oswal Pumps to set up 1.2 GW TOPCon solar cell manufacturing facility - AgroSpectrum India
Oswal Pumps plans to build a 1.2 GW TOPCon solar cell plant to feed its solar pumping business. Backward integration into cell manufacturing insulates margins against imported cell price swings under the central PM-KUSUM deployment scheme. For listed solar pump manufacturers such as Shakti Pumps, the expansion signals intensifying domestic supply capacity and potential margin compression in upcoming state agricultural tenders.
Green energy & solarSolar and green energy
DEE Development Engineers signs nuclear power framework agreement - Power Peak Digest
DEE Development Engineers finalized a framework pact with an EPC partner to deliver specialized pre-fabricated piping for nuclear power units. The agreement positions DEE as a preferred tier-two vendor as Nuclear Power Corporation of India tenders long-lead mechanical packages for indigenous 700 MW reactors. Firm purchase orders reported in subsequent quarterly filings will confirm the translation of this pact into revenue.
NuclearNuclear and SMR
Global uranium production to dip by 50% by 2040 as demand set to double, says IAEA report; forecast could - The Times of India
The International Atomic Energy Agency warned that primary uranium mine output will drop 50% by 2040 while reactor demand doubles. Because India imports over 80% of its civilian nuclear fuel, long-term global supply deficits will drive up feedstock procurement costs and inventory carrying requirements. Sustained fuel cost inflation risks delaying return profiles for domestic nuclear fleet expansions and associated equipment vendors.

Accenture looks to sell Chinese operations for up to $1.5 billion, FT reports
Accenture is exploring the sale of its mainland Chinese operations for up to $1.5 billion due to geopolitical friction and sluggish enterprise demand. The retreat reinforces corporate de-risking from China, yet offers limited direct revenue upside for Indian IT majors like TCS and Infosys given their negligible mainland exposure. Asia-Pacific enterprise IT contract announcements will confirm whether client budgets are redirecting to alternate delivery hubs.
Reuters Business · +1 other
Veteran SIP investors not deterred by stagnant market: Kotak Mahindra's's Harsha Upadhyaya
Monthly systematic investment plan inflows continue to hold above historical averages despite rate volatility and broader market consolidation. This persistent domestic liquidity buffers benchmark valuations against foreign portfolio outflows, directly supporting asset management companies like HDFC AMC and Nippon Life India through expanding assets under management. Upcoming monthly AMFI disbursement data will confirm whether net equity inflows withstand ongoing volatility in broader indices.
Mint Markets
Pharma Q2 Outlook: Pricing pressure, US competition to weigh on select players
Second-quarter earnings for domestic pharmaceutical exporters will diverge sharply as intensifying US price competition and generic Revlimid volume tapering compress base margins. Sun Pharma and Aurobindo benefit from specialty formulations and injectable demand, whereas Dr. Reddy’s and Lupin face operating margin compression on key generic molecules. US FDA inspection outcomes and oral-solid pricing data in upcoming quarterly filings will dictate full-year earnings revisions.

Companies and earnings
Australia's Ampol third-quarter Lytton refining margin more than doubles
Ampol reported a sharp quarter-on-quarter recovery in its Lytton refining margin to signal firm regional product spreads across the Asia-Pacific. Higher regional margins typically read across to Indian refiners such as Reliance Industries, BPCL, and IOCL, supporting their gross refining margins and downstream earnings. Weekly Singapore refining crack data will confirm if middle-distillate strength persists into the next quarter.
Reuters Business
Vedanta doubles South Africa zinc production capacity to 500,000 tonnes with $600 million investment
Vedanta expanded annual zinc production capacity at its South African Gamsberg mine to 500,000 tonnes through a $600 million investment. The added volume increases Zinc International's contribution to consolidated operating profit, generating foreign currency cash flows to help service holding company debt. London Metal Exchange cash zinc prices over the next quarter will determine the real payback on this expanded capacity.
Mint Companies · +1 other
IIFL Finance plans to raise ₹2,500-5,000 crore by selling stake amid Fairfax exit rumors
IIFL Finance plans to raise ₹2,500 to ₹5,000 crore in fresh equity capital, alongside promoter warrant subscriptions to limit dilution. The fundraise strengthens tier-1 capital ratios following regulatory curbs on its gold-loan business, while addressing supply overhang from Fairfax Financial's planned regulatory exit. Final issue pricing and terms will indicate the exact book value dilution for existing public shareholders.
ET Markets
Anup Bagchi backs 'exceptional' team as he connects the dots at HDFC Bank
Leadership changes at India's largest private lender will focus on managing balance sheet profitability and high post-merger loan-to-deposit ratios. Deposit mobilization remains the crucial operational lever determining credit growth and net interest margins for HDFC Bank over the current fiscal year. Official exchange filings will confirm the executive appointments and any realignment of the bank's operational priorities.
ET Markets
Geopolitics
Global Market Today: Asian shares fall as AI spending worries weigh on sentiment
Crude oil prices softened after the United States considered sanction waivers on Russian supplies, offsetting broader Asian equity weakness from technology sector valuation concerns. Lower oil prices reduce India's import bill, easing pressure on the rupee and trimming input costs for domestic paint, adhesive, and chemical manufacturers. Daily foreign portfolio investment flows will reveal whether cheaper crude arrests recent foreign selling.
ET Markets
India a keystone for Hitachi Energy supply chain amid global power crunch: CEO
Hitachi Energy is scaling its Indian manufacturing to ease global grid equipment shortages caused by data centre and industrial power demand. This expands export order inflows and execution visibility for Hitachi Energy India, while supporting operating margins across transmission peers like Siemens and ABB India. Watch quarterly order inflows to verify whether export bookings are sustaining their premium over domestic execution.
Mint Companies
Exporters may be asked to monitor supply chains' indirect emissions
The commerce ministry has begun discussions to mandate Scope 3 supply chain emissions tracking for Indian exporters. Compliance will lift administrative costs and capital expenditure across upstream vendors, pressuring margins for steel, aluminium, and chemicals exporters. Large producers such as Tata Steel and Hindalco must now audit tier-two suppliers to protect European market share ahead of financial penalties under the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism.
